target.title: fix(google): bound OAuth response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Three Google OAuth modules read HTTP response bodies without size limits, creating OOM risk when upstream services return oversized or malicious payloads.

**Solution**: Replace all unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()`, `.json()`, and `response.text()` calls with bounded SDK helpers (`readResponseWithLimit`, `readProviderJsonResponse`) that enforce configurable size caps.

**What changed**: `extensions/google/vertex-adc.ts`, `extensions/google/oauth.token.ts`, `extensions/google/oauth.project.ts` — 3 files, +25/-11 lines. All unbounded HTTP response reads replaced with bounded SDK helpers.

**What did NOT change**: No behavior change for well-formed responses under the size limits. No API or config surface changes. No dependency additions. Both helpers are already exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`.

## What Problem This Solves

Three distinct OAuth HTTP response paths in the Google plugin consume external response bodies without any size guard:

| File | Line(s) | Pattern | Risk |
|------|---------|---------|------|
| `vertex-adc.ts` | 280 | `Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer())` | OAuth token endpoint |
| `oauth.token.ts` | 39 | `(await response.json()) as {...}` | Token grant endpoint |
| `oauth.project.ts` | 24, 77, 138, 149, 214 | `(await response.json()) as {...}` | Multiple endpoints |

7 call sites across 3 files, all consuming unbounded HTTP response bodies. This is the same unbounded-read class that has been fixed across 30+ providers via the Plugin SDK. The Google OAuth paths were missed in those sweeps.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Bounded HTTP response reads for Google OAuth HTTP paths.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, `extensions/google/` test suite.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# run google tests via pnpm
pnpm test extensions/google -- --reporter verbose
pnpm test:changed
```

**After-fix evidence**: All 378 tests pass across 28 test files. All 228 `test:changed` tests pass across 15 test files.
```terminal_output
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/... (28 test files, 378 tests passed)
 ✓ |extension-providers| test:changed (15 test files, 228 tests passed)
```

BEFORE FIX — unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()` reads entire body into memory:
```typescript
const bytes = Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer());
```

AFTER FIX — bounded read with 1 MB cap and overflow error handling:
```typescript
const bytes = await readResponseWithLimit(response, GOOGLE_OAUTH_TOKEN_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES, {
  onOverflow: ({ maxBytes }) =>
    new Error(`Google OAuth token response exceeds ${maxBytes} bytes`),
});
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All Google extension tests pass with no regressions. Code compiles cleanly with no type errors.

**What was not tested**: Actual Google OAuth HTTP round-trips (requires live credentials). The SDK helpers themselves are integration-tested in `src/agents/provider-http-errors.test.ts`. This PR only swaps the call sites, preserving all existing error handling and test seams.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — bounded-read wrapper replaces unbounded call with same return type and compatible error semantics
- [x] No behavior change for normal-sized responses under the cap
- [x] No API, config, or dependency changes
- [x] Existing tests green (28 test files, 378 tests; 15 test:changed files, 228 tests)
- [x] SDK helpers are already shipped and used by 30+ other providers to prevent OOM
